title: Atrial fibrillation: type, history and anticoagulation
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's atrial fibrillation and related long-term drug therapy.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for persistent atrial fibrillation.

HPI
The patient is an 86-year-old male presenting today for a follow-up evaluation of persistent AFib. He reports that his heart rate remains relatively stable on his current regimen. He denies any episodes of lightheadedness, syncope, or significant palpitations. He notes some occasional fatigue but states his functional capacity remains unchanged. He does not report any shortness of breath during his daily activities. He is currently managed with rate-control medication and has not required any changes to his dosage recently. He denies any chest pain or associated symptoms of tachycardia.

Review of Systems
The patient reports no recent fevers, chills, or cough. He denies any unintentional weight loss or night sweats. He reports no changes in bowel habits or urinary frequency. He denies any new-onset numbness or weakness in his extremities. He denies any recent falls or acute injuries.

Social History
The patient lives at home with his spouse. He is retired and enjoys gardening and watching television. He reports a limited alcohol intake and denies any tobacco use.

Family History
His father had hypertension and a history of coronary artery disease. His mother had type 2 diabetes.

Medication List
Metoprolol 50mg daily
Lisinopril 10mg daily
Atorvastatin 20mg daily

Exam
The patient appears well-nourished and in no acute distress. He is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. His skin is warm and dry with no cyanosis or edema. Heart rate is regular but fast at 88 beats per minute. Rhythm is irregular. Blood pressure is 132/82 mmHg. Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. Abdomen is soft, non-tender, and non-distended. Extremities are symmetric with no visible swelling.

Vitals
Temperature: 98.4 F
Blood Pressure: 132/82 mmHg
Heart Rate: 88 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
SpO2: 97% on room air

Recent Labs
Hemoglobin: 13.5 g/dL
White Blood Cell Count: 7.2 x 10^9/L
Glucose: 108 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL
eGFR: 72 mL/min/1.73m2

Assessment
1. Persistent atrial fibrillation: The patient's condition is currently being managed with rate-control therapy. His heart rate is well-controlled. Given his low clinical risk profile, he does not require any anticoagulant.

Plan
1. Continue current metoprolol dosage for rate control of his persistent AFib.
2. Continue current blood pressure and cholesterol medications.
3. Patient to continue monitoring for any new symptoms of tachycardia.
4. Follow up in three months for a repeat evaluation.

Electronically signed, P. O'Brien, PA-C, 05/12/2026
explanations: Persistent atrial fibrillation, not documented as longstanding: I48.19, other persistent (HCC 238).
